discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the superfluid-Mott insulator transition to single-atom-resolved quantum gas microscopy

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München and Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Zoller and co-workers predicted in 1998 that atoms in optical lattices realize the Hubbard model with tunable parameters. In 2002, Greiner, Bloch and colleagues observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator, turning Feynman's idea of a quantum simulator into a laboratory tool. Greiner and Bloch then built quantum gas microscopes that image and address individual atoms in a lattice. With them, Mott shells, antiferromagnetic correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, string order, entanglement entropy and many-body localization have all been made directly visible, one atom at a time. This programme showed that complex quantum matter can be assembled and read out from the bottom up with complete control. It created a new branch of physics that links condensed matter, quantum information and atomic physics, and it underpins today's analog and digital neutral-atom quantum processors.
